Season shredded cooked chicken with lemon juice, black pepper and mint.
Place a small portion of chicken on each cucumber strip and roll up.
Secure with a toothpick if needed and serve fresh.

recipe_name: Boiled Eggs with Pumpkin Seeds
description: Simple boiled eggs topped with a sprinkle of roasted pumpkin seeds for added crunch and zinc.Egg protein supplies the amino acids needed to rebuild hair keratin and support skin repair.Pumpkin seeds add zinc, a key mineral for reducing hair fall and supporting healthy hair growth.
preparation_steps: Boil the eggs, peel and halve.
Sprinkle with roasted pumpkin seeds, black pepper and salt.
Serve fresh.

recipe_name: Watermelon Mint Hydration Bowl
description:
A hydrating bowl of fresh watermelon cubes tossed with mint leaves and a squeeze of lime.
Watermelon's high water content and lycopene support skin hydration and protect against oxidative stress.
Mint's cooling properties help calm skin inflammation, supporting a clearer, more even complexion.
preparation_steps: Cube the watermelon.
Toss with chopped mint leaves and lime juice.
Serve fresh and chilled.

recipe_name: Horse Gram Lunch Bowl (Huruli Oota) with Cucumber Salad
description:
A traditional horse gram curry served with rice, a vegetable stir-fry and a fresh salad.
Horse gram is one of the richest plant sources of protein and iron, directly supporting hair follicle strength and reducing hair fall.
Its high fibre content supports gut health and detoxification, which reflects in clearer, less acne-prone skin.
preparation_steps: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, sauté onion until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste, tomato and spice powders; cook until the masala thickens.
Add boiled horse gram with ½ cup water; simmer for 10–12 minutes until well coated.
Stir-fry mixed vegetables with a pinch of mustard seeds and grated coconut until just tender.
Toss cucumber with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve rice with horse gram curry, vegetable stir-fry and cucumber salad.

recipe_name: Pesarapappu and Gongura Meal with Onion Salad
description:
A wholesome meal of moong dal curry paired with tangy gongura (sorrel) leaves preparation, rice and a fresh salad.
Moong dal provides easily digestible plant protein and zinc, supporting collagen repair and hair follicle strength.
Gongura's high vitamin C and iron content supports scalp circulation and helps delay premature greying.
preparation_steps: Pressure cook moong dal with turmeric until soft; mash lightly and temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves in ½ tsp oil.
Sauté gongura leaves with dry red chili and garlic until wilted; cool and grind coarsely.
Temper the gongura chutney with mustard seeds in ½ tsp oil.
Toss onion with lemon juice and green chili for the salad.
Serve rice with pesarapappu, gongura chutney and onion salad.

recipe_name: Egg and Drumstick Sambar Lunch with Cucumber-Tomato Salad
description:
Steamed rice served with a protein-rich egg and drumstick sambar and a fresh vegetable salad.
Egg protein and selenium support hair keratin rebuilding, while drumstick's high iron and vitamin C content boosts scalp circulation.
The toor dal in the sambar provides folate and plant protein, both essential for reducing hair fall and supporting skin repair.
preparation_steps: Pressure cook toor dal with turmeric until soft; mash lightly.
Cook drumstick with tamarind pulp and sambar powder in 1 cup water until tender; add the cooked dal and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add boiled egg halves to the sambar and simmer for 2 minutes.
Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves in ½ tsp oil and pour over.
Toss cucumber and tomato with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve rice with egg and drumstick sambar and the salad.

recipe_name: Millet Lemon Rice with Peanut-Curry Leaf Powder and Cucumber Salad
description:
A tangy lemon-tempered millet rice served with a crunchy peanut and curry leaf powder and a fresh salad.
Millet's zinc and B-vitamins support scalp health and hair strength, while curry leaf powder's copper content helps maintain natural hair pigmentation.
Peanuts add vitamin E that protects skin from oxidative stress, supporting a healthy glow.
preparation_steps: Cook millet until fluffy and cool slightly.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and turmeric; pour over the cooked millet.
Add lemon juice and toss well; season with salt.
Dry roast curry leaves, peanuts, chana dal and red chili separately; cool and grind coarsely into a powder.
Toss cucumber with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve millet lemon rice with peanut-curry leaf powder and cucumber salad.

recipe_name: Egg Gassi Lunch with Onion-Tomato Salad
description:
A rich, roasted coconut-based egg curry served with steamed rice and a fresh salad.
Egg protein and choline support hair strand strength, while coconut's healthy fats help keep skin supple and hydrated.
The roasted spices in the gassi provide anti-inflammatory compounds that help calm skin redness and support a clearer complexion.
preparation_steps: Dry roast coconut, coriander seeds and Kashmiri red chili until golden; cool and grind with a little water into a smooth paste.
Heat coconut oil, sauté onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato; cook until soft.
Add the ground coconut paste and tamarind with 1 cup water; simmer for 10 minutes.
Add boiled egg halves and simmer for 3–4 minutes.
Toss onion and tomato with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve rice with egg gassi and the salad.

recipe_name: Avial and Adai Protein Lunch
description:
A traditional mixed vegetable avial in coconut-curd gravy served with protein-rich multi-lentil adai crepes.
The multi-lentil adai provides biotin and plant protein that support collagen synthesis and reduce hair fall.
Mixed vegetables in the avial deliver vitamin A and antioxidants that support skin cell renewal and a radiant complexion.
preparation_steps: Boil mixed vegetables with turmeric until just tender.
Grind coconut, cumin and green chili into a coarse paste; add to the vegetables along with curd and simmer gently for 2–3 minutes (do not boil hard).
Finish with raw coconut oil and curry leaves.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of adai batter and spread into a slightly thick crepe; drizzle oil and cook both sides until golden and crisp.
Serve adai with avial.

recipe_name: Curry Leaf Egg Rice Bowl with Broccoli Soup
description:
A fragrant curry leaf-tempered egg rice bowl served alongside a warming broccoli soup.
Curry leaves are rich in copper and antioxidants that support natural hair pigmentation and reduce premature greying.
Broccoli's vitamin C and sulforaphane support collagen synthesis and protect skin cells from oxidative damage.
preparation_steps: Heat oil, fry curry leaves until crisp; add mustard seeds and turmeric.
Scramble the egg into the pan, season with salt and toss with the cooked rice until well combined.
For the soup, sauté onion and garlic in ½ tsp oil until soft; add broccoli and stock, simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend until smooth, stir in black pepper and season with salt.
Serve the curry leaf egg rice bowl with a cup of broccoli soup.

recipe_name: Skin Glow South Indian Lunch with Tomato-Pomegranate Salad
description:
A balanced lunch plate of red rice, carrot-spinach dal, probiotic curd and a tomato-pomegranate salad designed for skin radiance.
Red rice's antioxidants and spinach's iron together support cellular skin repair and improve circulation to the scalp.
Pomegranate's polyphenols and curd's probiotics work together to fight free-radical skin damage and support a clear, glowing complexion.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Pigmentation, Fine lines & ageing, Glow)
preparation_steps: Pressure cook toor dal with turmeric until soft; mash.
Sauté grated carrot in ½ tsp oil for 2 minutes; add spinach and cook until wilted; mix into the dal and simmer for 5 minutes.
Temper with cumin in ½ tsp oil and pour over.
Toss tomato, pomegranate and mint with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve red rice with carrot-spinach dal, curd and the salad.

recipe_name: Kosambari Protein Plate
description:
A traditional raw moong dal and vegetable salad served alongside a protein-rich paneer dish and rice.
Soaked raw moong dal provides plant protein and folate that support hair growth and collagen synthesis for skin repair.
The raw vegetables add hydration and vitamin C that support skin elasticity and a clear, healthy complexion.
preparation_steps: Sauté paneer cubes in ½ tsp oil with turmeric and chili powder until lightly golden; set aside.
Drain soaked moong dal and combine with grated cucumber and carrot.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in ½ tsp oil; mix into the kosambari.
Stir in grated coconut and lemon juice; season with salt.
Serve rice with paneer stir-fry and kosambari.

recipe_name: Methi Egg Kuzhambu with Red Rice and Cucumber Salad
description:
A tangy tamarind gravy made with fresh fenugreek leaves and boiled eggs, served with red rice and a cucumber salad.
Fenugreek's iron and nicotinic acid strengthen hair strands and improve scalp circulation, reducing hair fall.
Egg protein supports keratin rebuilding, while red rice's antioxidants protect skin cells from oxidative stress.
preparation_steps: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and curry leaves; sauté onion until golden.
Add methi leaves and cook until wilted.
Add tamarind pulp, kuzhambu powder and 1 cup water; simmer for 10 minutes.
Add boiled egg halves and simmer for 3 minutes.
Toss cucumber with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve red rice with methi egg kuzhambu and the salad.

recipe_name: Ragi Sangati with Chicken Pulusu and Onion-Tomato Salad
description:
A traditional finger-millet mash served with a tangy tamarind-based lean chicken curry and a fresh salad.
Ragi's calcium and iron strengthen hair roots, while chicken breast's lean protein provides the amino acids needed to rebuild hair keratin.
Tamarind in the pulusu supplies vitamin C that boosts collagen synthesis and supports skin firmness.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Fine lines & ageing, Collagen boost)
preparation_steps: Bring water to a boil; slowly stir in ragi flour, cook on low heat for 8–10 minutes stirring continuously; shape into a mound.
Heat oil, sauté onion and curry leaves until golden; add ginger-garlic paste, tomato and spice powders.
Add chicken and sear for 2–3 minutes; add tamarind pulp and ¾ cup water; cover and simmer for 15 minutes until cooked through.
Toss onion and tomato with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve ragi sangati with chicken pulusu and the salad.

recipe_name: Ulava Charu Meal with Cucumber Salad
description:
A traditional horse gram rasam-style soup served with rice, a vegetable stir-fry and a fresh salad.
Horse gram is exceptionally protein and iron-rich, directly supporting hair follicle strength and reducing hair fall.
Its high fibre and antioxidant content supports gut health and gentle detoxification, contributing to clearer, healthier skin.
preparation_steps: Pressure cook horse gram until soft; mash slightly and strain the liquid for the rasam base.
Simmer the horse gram liquid with tamarind pulp, cumin, pepper and garlic for 10 minutes.
Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves in ½ tsp oil and pour over.
Stir-fry mixed vegetables with a pinch of mustard seeds until tender.
Toss cucumber with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve rice with ulava charu, vegetable stir-fry and salad.

recipe_name: Pepper Chicken Millet Plate with Cucumber-Tomato Salad
description:
A fragrant, freshly ground pepper-spiced chicken curry served with fibre-rich millet and a fresh salad.
Lean chicken breast delivers high-quality protein essential for rebuilding hair keratin and reducing breakage.
Black pepper's piperine boosts nutrient absorption and provides anti-inflammatory benefits that help calm skin redness.
preparation_steps: Heat oil, sauté onion and curry leaves until golden; add ginger-garlic paste and fennel seeds.
Add tomato, crushed pepper and coriander powder; cook until the masala thickens.
Add chicken, sear for 2–3 minutes, then add ½ cup water; cover and simmer for 15 minutes until cooked through (internal temp 75°C).
Toss cucumber and tomato with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve foxtail millet with pepper chicken and the salad.

recipe_name: Murungai Keerai Kootu Lunch with Tomato Salad
description:
A traditional drumstick leaves and lentil coconut stew served with steamed rice and a fresh salad.
Drumstick leaves are among the richest plant sources of iron, calcium and vitamin C, supporting hair follicle strength and collagen production.
The coconut and lentil combination provides healthy fats and plant protein that support skin barrier integrity and a radiant complexion.
preparation_steps: Pressure cook toor dal until soft; mash slightly.
Grind coconut, cumin and green chili into a coarse paste.
Mix drumstick leaves into the mashed dal and simmer for 5–6 minutes until leaves are cooked through.
Stir in the coconut paste and simmer for 2 minutes; season with salt.
Temper with mustard seeds, urad dal and curry leaves in coconut oil and mix through.
Toss tomato with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve rice with murungai keerai kootu and tomato salad.

recipe_name: Hair Vitality Lunch Plate
description:
A nourishing lunch plate of brown rice, iron-rich methi dal, sautéed spinach and a protein-rich egg, designed for hair strength.
Fenugreek in the dal and spinach's iron work together to boost scalp circulation and reduce hair fall.
Egg's biotin and selenium support keratin production and protect the scalp from oxidative stress.
primary_goal: Hair repair (Hair fall, Dandruff, Greying hair)
preparation_steps: Pressure cook toor dal with turmeric until soft; mash lightly.
Sauté methi leaves in ½ tsp oil until wilted; add to the dal and simmer for 5 minutes.
Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves in ½ tsp oil.
In a separate pan, sauté spinach with garlic in ½ tsp oil until wilted.
Boil and peel the egg.
Serve brown rice with methi dal, sautéed spinach and the boiled egg.

recipe_name: High-Protein South Indian Beauty Bowl
description:
A balanced beauty bowl of millet, paneer tikka, sprouted moong and a coconut-cucumber raita.
Paneer and sprouted moong together provide a powerful plant and dairy protein combination to support both hair keratin and skin collagen.
Sprouted moong's vitamin E and raita's probiotics support skin barrier repair and gut health linked to a clear, radiant complexion.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Fine lines & ageing, Pores & texture)
preparation_steps: Pan-grill marinated paneer cubes in ½ tsp oil until lightly golden on all sides.
Lightly steam sprouted moong for 2–3 minutes; toss with lemon juice.
Mix curd, grated cucumber, coconut and roasted cumin for the raita.
Serve millet topped with paneer tikka and sprouted moong, with coconut-cucumber raita on the side.

recipe_name: Methi Tomato Pulao with Carrot-Cucumber Raita
description:
A fragrant one-pot brown rice pulao cooked with fresh fenugreek leaves and tomatoes, served with a cooling carrot-cucumber raita.
Fenugreek's iron and nicotinic acid support scalp circulation and strengthen hair strands, reducing hair fall.
Curd in the raita provides probiotics that support gut health, which is directly linked to clearer, calmer skin.
preparation_steps: Heat oil, sauté whole spices and onion until golden; add ginger-garlic paste, tomato and methi leaves.
Cook until methi wilts and tomato softens.
Add washed rice with 1 cup water; cover and cook until rice is fully cooked and water absorbed.
Mix curd, grated carrot, cucumber and cumin powder for the raita.
Serve methi tomato pulao with carrot-cucumber raita.

recipe_name: Tomato Bath with Raita and Broccoli Curry
description:
A tangy one-pot tomato rice served with a cooling curd raita and a nutrient-dense broccoli curry.
Tomato's lycopene protects skin from sun-related oxidative damage, while broccoli's sulforaphane and vitamin C support collagen synthesis.
Curd's probiotics in the raita support gut health, which is closely tied to reducing skin breakouts.
preparation_steps: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste.
Add tomato and cook until soft; add washed rice with 1 cup water, cover and cook until done.
Whisk curd with mint and a pinch of salt for the raita.
Sauté onion for the broccoli curry, add broccoli florets with turmeric and cumin, cover and cook 6–8 minutes until tender.
Serve tomato bath with curd raita and broccoli curry.

recipe_name: Huli Avalakki Lunch Bowl with Cucumber-Tomato Salad
description:
A tangy tamarind-soaked flattened rice dish tempered with mustard seeds and peanuts, served as a light lunch bowl.
Peanuts provide vitamin E and biotin that protect skin cells and support hair strand strength.
Tamarind's vitamin C content supports collagen synthesis for firmer skin, while the fibre in the flattened rice aids digestion linked to clearer skin.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Fine lines & ageing, Collagen boost)
preparation_steps: Rinse poha briefly and drain; let it soften for 5 minutes.
Mix tamarind pulp and jaggery with the softened poha.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, add turmeric and chili powder; add the poha mixture and toss well for 3–4 minutes.
Add roasted peanuts and toss.
Toss cucumber and tomato with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve huli avalakki with the salad.

recipe_name: Rice with Mushroom Coconut Curry, Fish Curry and Curd
description:
A wholesome lunch of steamed rice with a creamy mushroom coconut curry, light fish curry and probiotic curd.
Fish omega-3 fatty acids reduce skin inflammation and support a smoother complexion, while mushroom's biotin and vitamin D support scalp health and hair growth.
Curd's probiotics strengthen the gut-skin axis for clearer skin and fish lean protein provides amino acids essential for hair keratin rebuilding.
preparation_steps: Heat ½ tsp oil, add curry leaves, onion and ginger-garlic paste for fish curry; sauté until golden.
Add tomato, turmeric and red chili powder; cook until soft.
Add fish cubes and water; simmer gently for 8 minutes until fish is cooked through; season with salt.
Sauté onion and ginger in coconut oil for mushroom curry; add mushrooms and cook until tender.
Add coconut milk and simmer gently for 4–5 minutes; season with salt.
Serve steamed rice with mushroom coconut curry, fish curry and curd.

recipe_name: Bisibele Bath with Kosambari, Amla-Coriander Chutney and Spiced Buttermilk
description:
A traditional one-pot rice, lentil and vegetable dish served with a raw moong salad, amla chutney and spiced buttermilk.
The toor dal and vegetables in bisibele bath provide plant protein and antioxidants that support skin repair and hair health.
Amla's vitamin C in the chutney boosts collagen synthesis, while buttermilk's probiotics support gut health linked to clearer skin.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Fine lines & ageing, Pores & texture)
preparation_steps: Pressure cook rice, dal and vegetables with bisibele bath powder and tamarind until soft; mash slightly and finish with ghee.
Combine soaked moong dal, carrot, cucumber, coconut and lemon juice for the kosambari.
Blend amla, coriander and green chili with a little water into a smooth chutney.
Whisk buttermilk with cumin and ginger.
Serve bisibele bath with kosambari, amla-coriander chutney and spiced buttermilk.

recipe_name: Brown Rice with Drumstick Sambar, Beans Poriyal, Carrot Kosambari, Amla Chutney and Curd
description:
A complete traditional South Indian meal with drumstick sambar, coconut beans poriyal, carrot kosambari, amla chutney and curd.
Drumstick's iron and vitamin C improve scalp circulation, while amla's exceptional vitamin C content supports collagen synthesis for skin and hair.
Curd's probiotics and the fibre from vegetables support gut health, reflecting in clearer, healthier skin.
preparation_steps: Pressure cook toor dal with turmeric; add drumstick, tamarind and sambar powder with water and simmer 10 minutes; temper.
Cook beans until tender; stir in coconut for the poriyal.
Mix grated carrot and soaked moong dal with lemon juice for kosambari.
Blend amla and green chili with a little water for the chutney.
Whisk curd until smooth.
Serve brown rice with all the accompaniments.

recipe_name: Red Rice with Cow Pea Curry, Pumpkin Stir-Fry and Tomato-Onion-Lemon Salad
description:
A hearty meal of red rice with a protein-rich cow pea curry, a light pumpkin stir-fry and a tangy salad.
Cow peas are rich in plant protein and iron, supporting hair follicle strength and reducing hair fall.
Pumpkin's beta-carotene supports skin cell renewal, while the fresh salad's vitamin C boosts collagen production.
preparation_steps: Heat oil, sauté onion, add ginger-garlic paste, tomato, turmeric and chili powder; cook until soft.
Add boiled cow peas with ½ cup water; simmer for 8 minutes.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in ½ tsp oil; sauté pumpkin until tender and lightly golden.
Toss tomato, onion and lemon juice for the salad.
Serve red rice with cow pea curry, pumpkin stir-fry and salad.

recipe_name: Steamed Rice with Fish Curry, Okra Poriyal, Buttermilk and Cucumber Salad
description:
A balanced South Indian meal of steamed rice with a tangy fish curry, dry okra stir-fry, probiotic buttermilk and fresh cucumber salad.
Fish omega-3 fatty acids reduce skin inflammation and support a smoother complexion, while lean fish protein provides amino acids essential for hair keratin rebuilding.
Buttermilk's probiotics support the gut-skin axis for clearer skin and okra's vitamin C boosts collagen production for skin firmness and elasticity.
preparation_steps: Heat oil, add curry leaves and onion for fish curry; sauté until golden; add ginger-garlic paste, tomato, turmeric and chili powder; cook until soft.
Add tamarind pulp, fish cubes and water; simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until fish is cooked through; season with salt.
Cook okra with onion in ½ tsp oil on medium heat uncovered until dry and tender; season with salt.
Whisk buttermilk with cumin and ginger.
Toss cucumber with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve rice with fish curry, okra poriyal, buttermilk and cucumber salad.

recipe_name: Steamed Rice with Pumpkin Coconut Curry, Rasam, Buttermilk and Carrot Salad
description:
A comforting meal of steamed rice with a sweet pumpkin coconut curry, pepper rasam, buttermilk and a carrot salad.
Pumpkin's beta-carotene converts to vitamin A, supporting skin cell renewal and a healthy scalp environment.
Rasam's black pepper boosts nutrient absorption, while buttermilk's probiotics support gut health linked to clearer skin.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Aging skin, Fine lines & ageing, Cell renewal)
preparation_steps: Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in coconut oil; add pumpkin and cook until tender; add coconut milk and simmer gently for 3–4 minutes.
Simmer tomato, tamarind, pepper and cumin in 1 cup water for 10 minutes for the rasam; strain.
Whisk buttermilk with ginger.
Toss grated carrot with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve rice with pumpkin coconut curry, rasam, buttermilk and carrot salad.

recipe_name: Pothichoru with Cucumber-Tomato Salad
description:
A traditional packed rice meal of banana-leaf wrapped rice with mixed accompaniments and a fresh salad.
The banana leaf infuses the rice with polyphenols, while the mixed dal and vegetable accompaniments provide protein, fibre and antioxidants for skin and hair health.
The fresh salad's vitamin C and hydration support collagen production and skin elasticity.
preparation_steps: Warm banana leaf over a flame until pliable and fragrant.
Place a portion of rice on the leaf, add dal curry, vegetable stir-fry, curd and a small amount of pickle.
Wrap or fold the banana leaf over the meal.
Toss cucumber and tomato with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve the pothichoru on the banana leaf with the salad on the side.

recipe_name: Steamed Rice with Prawn Tomato Curry, Ginger Rasam, Buttermilk and Cucumber
description:
A protein-rich lunch of steamed rice with a tangy prawn-tomato curry, digestive ginger rasam, probiotic buttermilk and fresh cucumber.
Prawns provide zinc and lean protein essential for hair keratin production and reducing hair fall.
Tomato's lycopene protects skin from oxidative damage, while ginger rasam supports digestion for clearer, healthier skin.
preparation_steps: Heat oil, sauté onion, add ginger-garlic paste, tomato, turmeric and chili powder; cook until soft.
Add prawns and cook for 3–4 minutes until just opaque; season with salt.
Simmer ginger, tomato, pepper and cumin in 1 cup water for 10 minutes for the rasam; strain.
Whisk buttermilk and slice cucumber with lemon juice.
Serve rice with prawn tomato curry, ginger rasam, buttermilk and cucumber.

recipe_name: Vegetable Soup with Curry Leaf Green Rice and Cucumber Raita
description:
A warming antioxidant-rich vegetable soup served alongside fragrant curry leaf green rice and a cooling cucumber raita.
Curry leaves' copper content supports natural hair pigmentation, while the mixed vegetable soup delivers vitamins A and C for skin repair.
Cucumber raita's probiotics and hydration support gut health and skin elasticity.
preparation_steps: Simmer vegetables, garlic and pepper in water for 12–15 minutes; blend partially and season with salt.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, add curry leaf paste and toss with cooked brown rice for 2–3 minutes.
Mix curd, grated cucumber and cumin for the raita.
Serve the vegetable soup with curry leaf green rice and cucumber raita.

recipe_name: Steamed Rice with Green Leafy Vegetable Fry, Vitamin C Source and Curd
description:
A nourishing complete meal of steamed rice, lightly sautéed green leafy vegetables, a fresh vitamin C fruit and probiotic curd.
Green leafy vegetables such as spinach, methi or moringa provide iron and folate that improve scalp circulation and reduce hair fall.
Vitamin C from guava or amla enhances iron absorption and supports collagen synthesis for skin firmness and elasticity.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Collagen boost, Fine lines & ageing)
preparation_steps: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, dry red chili and garlic; add the green leafy vegetable and sauté until wilted and cooked through.
Season with salt and a pinch of turmeric.
Whisk curd until smooth.
Slice guava or halve amla.
Serve steamed rice with green leafy vegetable fry, fresh vitamin C fruit and curd.

recipe_name: Rice with Ridge Gourd Curry, Green Peas Masala, Fish Fry, Buttermilk and Cucumber Salad
description:
A varied South Indian meal of rice with ridge gourd curry, spiced green peas, pan-fried fish, probiotic buttermilk and cucumber salad.
Fish omega-3 fatty acids reduce skin inflammation and support an even complexion, while lean fish protein provides amino acids essential for hair keratin rebuilding.
Green peas and field beans provide plant protein and iron for hair follicle strength, and buttermilk's probiotics support the gut-skin axis for clearer skin.
preparation_steps: Cook ridge gourd with toor dal, turmeric and a splash of water until soft; season with salt.
Sauté onion, add tomato, spice powders and green peas; cook until masala thickens.
In a separate pan, cook field beans with onion and spices until well coated.
Whisk buttermilk.
Toss cucumber with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve rice with all curries, buttermilk and cucumber salad.
Marinate fish fillet in turmeric, chili powder and lemon juice for 10 minutes.
Pan-fry in ½ tsp olive oil for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Serve alongside all curries, buttermilk and cucumber salad.

recipe_name: Ginger Pepper Chicken Lunch with Cucumber-Tomato Salad
description:
A warmly spiced ginger and black pepper chicken breast curry served with steamed rice, rasam and a fresh salad.
Lean chicken breast delivers high-quality protein and selenium essential for rebuilding hair keratin and protecting the scalp.
Black pepper and ginger together provide strong anti-inflammatory benefits that help calm skin redness and reduce acne.
preparation_steps: Heat oil, sauté onion, garlic and curry leaves until golden.
Add grated ginger, crushed pepper and turmeric; cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken, sear for 2–3 minutes, then add ½ cup water; cover and simmer for 15 minutes until cooked through (internal temp 75°C).
Simmer tomato, tamarind, pepper and cumin in 1 cup water for the rasam; strain.
Toss cucumber and tomato with lemon juice for the salad.
Serve rice with ginger pepper chicken, rasam and salad.

recipe_name: Millet with Mushroom Green Pea Curry and Spinach Soup
description:
A wholesome plate of foxtail millet with a mushroom and green pea curry served alongside a warming spinach soup.
Mushroom's vitamin D and biotin support scalp health, while green peas provide plant protein and zinc for hair follicle strength.
Spinach soup's iron and vitamin K support circulation and skin repair, contributing to a healthier, clearer complexion.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Collagen boost, Fine lines & ageing)
preparation_steps: Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste, add tomato, turmeric and cumin; cook until soft.
Add mushrooms and green peas; cook for 5–6 minutes until well coated.
Sauté garlic in ½ tsp oil, add spinach and wilt; add water and simmer 8 minutes; blend smooth and stir in pepper.
Serve foxtail millet with mushroom-green pea curry and spinach soup.

recipe_name: Brown Rice with Fish Curry, Beetroot Poriyal and Spiced Buttermilk
description:
A protein-rich lunch of brown rice with a light fish curry, iron-rich beetroot poriyal and probiotic spiced buttermilk.
Fish omega-3 fatty acids reduce skin inflammation and support a smoother, more even-toned complexion, while lean fish protein provides amino acids essential for hair keratin rebuilding.
Beetroot's iron and folate boost scalp circulation reducing hair fall, and buttermilk's probiotics support the gut-skin axis for clearer, healthier skin.
preparation_steps: Heat oil, add curry leaves and onion for fish curry; sauté until golden; add ginger-garlic paste, tomato and spice powders; cook until soft.
Add fish cubes and water; simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until fish is cooked through; season with salt.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in ½ tsp oil; add grated beetroot, cover and cook 5–6 minutes until tender; stir in coconut.
Whisk buttermilk with cumin, ginger and curry leaves.
Serve brown rice with fish curry, beetroot poriyal and spiced buttermilk.

recipe_name: Ragi Puttu with Ripe Plantain, Pumpkin Seeds and Boiled Egg
description:
A traditional steamed ragi puttu layered with shredded coconut, served with ripe plantain, pumpkin seeds and a boiled egg.

Ragi's calcium and iron strengthen hair roots and prevent premature greying, while egg protein supplies the amino acids needed to rebuild hair keratin and repair skin tissue.

Pumpkin seeds add zinc for keratin production and ripe plantain provides potassium and biotin that nourish hair strands and support skin hydration.
preparation_steps: Sprinkle water gradually into the ragi flour a little at a time, mixing with fingers until the flour is just moist and crumbly it should hold shape when pressed but not be wet or doughy.
Add a pinch of salt and mix well.
Layer the puttu maker alternately  a layer of shredded coconut, then a layer of moistened ragi flour, then coconut again, finishing with a coconut layer on top.
Steam the puttu for 8–10 minutes until cooked through and the steam rises consistently from the top.
Meanwhile, boil the egg, peel and halve.
Slice the ripe plantain into rounds.
Unmould the puttu onto a plate.
Serve the ragi puttu alongside the ripe plantain slices, pumpkin seeds and the boiled egg.

recipe_name: Kerala Fish Curry with Red Rice, Cucumber Raita and Onion Salad
description:
A traditional Kerala-style tangy coconut and tamarind fish curry served with red rice, cooling cucumber raita and a fresh onion salad.
Fish omega-3 fatty acids (EPA and DHA) directly reduce skin inflammation and support a smoother, more even-toned complexion, while lean fish protein provides all essential amino acids for hair keratin rebuilding and reducing hair fall.
Red rice's antioxidants protect skin cells from oxidative damage, and cucumber raita's probiotics strengthen the gut-skin axis for clearer, healthier skin.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Acne, Fine lines & ageing, Anti-inflammatory)
preparation_steps: Heat coconut oil in a clay pot or pan; add curry leaves and sliced onion; sauté until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste; cook for 1 minute; add tomato, fish curry powder and turmeric; cook until soft and fragrant.
Add tamarind pulp and ¾ cup water; bring to a simmer for 5 minutes.
Add fish pieces; simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until fish is cooked through and curry thickens.
Stir in coconut milk; simmer on low heat for 2 minutes   do not boil after adding coconut milk.
Mix curd, grated cucumber and cumin powder for the raita.
Toss sliced onion with lemon juice and green chili for the salad.
Serve hot red rice with Kerala fish curry, cucumber raita and onion salad.

recipe_name: Andhra Fish Pulusu with Foxtail Millet, Spinach-Onion Salad and Buttermilk
description:
A tangy Andhra-style tamarind-based fish curry (pulusu) served with fibre-rich foxtail millet, a fresh spinach-onion salad and digestive buttermilk.
Fish omega-3 fatty acids reduce scalp inflammation and support stronger hair follicles, while lean fish protein delivers amino acids directly for hair keratin synthesis and skin collagen repair.
Tamarind's vitamin C boosts iron absorption from the meal for better scalp circulation, and buttermilk's probiotics strengthen the gut-skin axis resulting in clearer, less acne-prone skin.
primary_goal: Hair repair (Hair fall, Keratin rebuild, Scalp health)
Skin repair (Acne, Fine lines & ageing, Collagen boost)
preparation_steps: Cook foxtail millet with 1½ cups water until fluffy; set aside.
Heat oil in a pan; temper mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and curry leaves.
Add onion and sauté until golden; add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add tomato, turmeric, red chili powder and coriander powder; cook until masala thickens and oil separates.
Add tamarind pulp and 1 cup water; bring to a gentle simmer for 5 minutes.
Add fish pieces; simmer on low heat for 8–10 minutes until fish is cooked through and gravy thickens; season with salt.
Toss baby spinach and sliced onion with lemon juice for the salad.
Whisk buttermilk with a pinch of grated ginger.
Serve foxtail millet with Andhra fish pulusu, spinach-onion salad and buttermilk.

recipe_name: Fresh Guava with Pumpkin Seed Sprinkle
description:
A single fresh guava is  a standalone snack.
Guava is one of the richest sources of vitamin C, which directly boosts collagen synthesis for firmer, more elastic skin.
It also supports scalp circulation and protects hair follicles from oxidative damage, helping reduce hair fall. Pumpkin seeds add zinc for keratin production and hair follicle strength, complementing guava's Vitamin C for collagen synthesis.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Fine lines & ageing, Collagen boost)
preparation_steps: Wash the guava thoroughly under running water.
Slice or eat whole as preferred.
Eat on an empty stomach or as a mid-evening snack.
For seed sprinkle: Sprinkle roasted pumpkin seeds over the sliced guava before eating.

recipe_name: Fresh Amla with Mixed Seed Sprinkle
description:
Two fresh amla eaten raw as a powerful skin and hair repair snack.
Amla contains the highest natural concentration of vitamin C among all fruits, which boosts collagen production and helps fade pigmentation.
Its antioxidants protect melanin-producing cells in hair follicles, helping delay premature greying and reduce hair fall. Mixed seeds add plant omega-3 and zinc, enhancing amla's Vitamin C for collagen synthesis and iron absorption.
preparation_steps: Wash the amla thoroughly.
Eat raw, sliced or whole.
Can be dipped in a pinch of rock salt if preferred.
For seed sprinkle: Grind seeds lightly; sprinkle over halved amla before eating.

recipe_name: Soaked Almonds
description:
Six overnight-soaked almonds is  a simple, nutrient-dense snack.
Almonds are rich in biotin and vitamin E, both of which strengthen hair strands and protect the scalp from oxidative stress.
Vitamin E also acts as a powerful antioxidant for skin, helping reduce fine lines and support a healthy skin barrier.
preparation_steps: Soak almonds in water overnight.
In the evening, drain and peel the skins if preferred.
Eat slowly as a snack.

recipe_name: Soaked Walnuts
description:
A small portion of soaked walnuts is  a brain and beauty snack.
Walnuts are exceptionally rich in omega-3 fatty acids, which reduce skin inflammation and help maintain a smooth, hydrated skin barrier.
Their biotin content also strengthens hair strands, reduces brittleness and supports healthier hair growth.
preparation_steps: Soak walnuts in water for 2 hours to reduce bitterness and improve digestibility.
Drain and eat slowly as a snack.

recipe_name: Pumpkin Seeds
description:
A small handful of lightly roasted pumpkin seeds is  a mineral-rich snack.
Pumpkin seeds are one of the best plant sources of zinc, a mineral essential for keratin production and reducing hair fall.
Their magnesium content also helps regulate hormones linked to hair loss and supports skin cell regeneration.
preparation_steps: Dry roast pumpkin seeds in a pan on low heat for 2–3 minutes until they pop lightly.
Cool and eat as a snack.
Can be eaten raw if preferred.

recipe_name: Sunflower Seeds
description:
A small portion of roasted sunflower seeds is  a vitamin E-rich snack.
Sunflower seeds are an excellent source of vitamin E, which protects skin cells from UV-related oxidative damage and maintains skin barrier health.
Their selenium content also protects hair follicles from damage and supports healthy hair growth.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Fine lines & ageing, Pores & texture)
preparation_steps: Dry roast sunflower seeds on low heat for 2–3 minutes until lightly golden.
Cool and eat as a snack.

recipe_name: Fresh Papaya Slices with Pumpkin Seed Sprinkle
description:
A small bowl of fresh ripe papaya slices is  a skin-renewing snack.
Papaya's vitamin A and papain enzyme support skin cell turnover, helping fade pigmentation and reveal a clearer, more even complexion.
Its vitamin C content also boosts collagen production for firmer skin and protects hair follicles from oxidative stress. Pumpkin seeds add zinc for keratin production, complementing papaya's Vitamin A and papain enzyme for skin cell renewal.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Pigmentation, Fine lines & ageing, Cell renewal)
preparation_steps: Peel and deseed the papaya.
Slice into bite-sized pieces.
Eat fresh as a snack.
For seed sprinkle: Slice papaya into a bowl; sprinkle roasted pumpkin seeds over the top before eating.

recipe_name: Pomegranate Arils with Flaxseed Sprinkle
description:
A small bowl of fresh pomegranate arils is  a powerful antioxidant snack.
Pomegranate's polyphenols fight skin-ageing free radicals and support collagen production for firmer, more youthful skin.
Its iron content also improves scalp circulation, helping reduce hair fall and support healthier hair growth. Ground flaxseeds add plant omega-3 fatty acids that reduce skin inflammation, complementing pomegranate's polyphenols for skin-ageing protection.
preparation_steps: Deseed the pomegranate and measure ½ cup of arils.
Eat fresh as a snack.
For seed sprinkle: Grind flaxseeds fresh; sprinkle over pomegranate arils before eating.

recipe_name: Fresh Orange with Pumpkin Seed Sprinkle
description:
A single fresh orange is  a vitamin C-rich skin-repair snack.
Orange's high vitamin C content is essential for collagen synthesis, directly supporting skin firmness and reducing fine lines.
Vitamin C also enhances iron absorption from meals, supporting better scalp circulation and reducing hair fall. Pumpkin seeds add zinc for keratin production, and their magnesium content complements orange's Vitamin C for maximum collagen activation.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Fine lines & ageing, Collagen boost)
preparation_steps: Peel the orange and separate into segments.
Eat fresh as a snack.
For seed sprinkle: Peel and segment the orange; sprinkle roasted pumpkin seeds alongside before eating.

recipe_name: Black Sesame Seeds
description:
A small portion of toasted black sesame seeds is  a traditional hair-nourishing snack.
Black sesame seeds are rich in calcium and copper, both of which support natural hair pigmentation and help reduce premature greying.
Their zinc and iron content also strengthens hair roots and supports healthy scalp circulation.
preparation_steps: Dry roast black sesame seeds in a pan on low heat for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Cool and eat as a snack.
Can be mixed with a pinch of jaggery powder if preferred.

recipe_name: Flaxseeds
description:
A small portion of ground flaxseeds taken with warm water as an omega-3-rich snack.
Flaxseeds are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and lignans, which reduce skin inflammation and maintain the skin barrier for a smooth, hydrated complexion.
Their plant-based omega-3s also nourish hair follicles and help reduce scalp dryness and hair breakage.
preparation_steps: Grind flaxseeds freshly in a small blender or spice grinder.
Stir into half a cup of warm water.
Drink or eat immediately (ground flaxseeds oxidise quickly, so consume fresh).

recipe_name: Soaked Dates with Sesame Seed Sprinkle
description:
Two to three soaked dates is  a natural iron-rich energy snack.
Dates are one of the richest natural sources of iron, directly supporting scalp circulation and helping reduce hair fall over time.
Their vitamin B5 and antioxidants also support skin cell renewal and help maintain a healthy, youthful complexion. Sesame seeds add calcium and copper that support natural hair pigmentation, complementing dates' iron for scalp circulation and hair growth.
preparation_steps: Soak dates in water for 30 minutes to soften.
Deseed and eat slowly as a snack.
For seed sprinkle: Toast sesame seeds lightly; sprinkle over soaked dates before eating.

recipe_name: Fresh Coconut Pieces with Pumpkin Seed Sprinkle
description:
A small portion of fresh tender coconut meat is  a healthy fat snack.
Fresh coconut is rich in medium-chain fatty acids that support skin barrier integrity and help maintain a smooth, hydrated complexion.
Its lauric acid has natural anti-inflammatory properties that calm scalp irritation and support a healthy environment for hair growth. Pumpkin seeds add zinc for keratin production, perfectly complementing coconut's lauric acid for scalp health and antimicrobial skin protection.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Fine lines & ageing, Pores & texture)
preparation_steps: Scoop the tender coconut meat from a fresh coconut.
Cut into small bite-sized pieces.
Eat fresh as a snack.
For seed sprinkle: Sprinkle pumpkin seeds over fresh coconut pieces before eating.

recipe_name: Roasted Chana with Mixed Seed Sprinkle
description:
A small portion of roasted dry chickpeas is  a protein-rich crunchy snack.
Roasted chana provides plant protein and biotin that strengthen hair strands and support keratin production.
Its high fibre content supports gut health, which is directly linked to reducing skin breakouts and improving complexion clarity. Mixed seeds add zinc and Vitamin E that protect skin cells and support keratin production, complementing chana's biotin for hair strand strength.
preparation_steps: Portion ¼ cup of roasted chana into a small bowl.
Sprinkle with a pinch of black pepper or chaat masala if preferred.
Eat as a crunchy snack.
For seed sprinkle: Mix roasted seeds into the chana before eating.

recipe_name: Fresh Cucumber Sticks with Pumpkin Seed Sprinkle
description:
Sliced fresh cucumber is a hydrating, cooling snack with a squeeze of lemon.
Cucumber's high water content and silica deeply hydrate skin cells, supporting elasticity and a plump, dewy complexion.
Its anti-inflammatory compounds help soothe scalp irritation and support a calm, healthy environment for hair growth. Pumpkin seeds add zinc for keratin production and hair follicle health, complementing cucumber's silica for skin elasticity and hydration.
preparation_steps: Wash the cucumber thoroughly.
Cut into sticks or rounds.
Sprinkle with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of black salt if preferred.
Eat fresh as a snack.
For seed sprinkle: Arrange cucumber sticks on a plate; sprinkle pumpkin seeds alongside with lemon and black salt.

recipe_name: Soaked Figs with Flaxseed Sprinkle
description:
Two soaked dried figs is  a naturally sweet iron and calcium-rich snack.
Figs are rich in iron and zinc, supporting scalp circulation and keratin production to reduce hair fall.
Their vitamin C and antioxidants also support collagen synthesis and skin cell renewal for a firmer, more radiant complexion. Ground flaxseeds add plant omega-3 fatty acids that reduce skin inflammation, complementing figs' iron and zinc for scalp circulation and hair growth.
preparation_steps: Soak dried figs in water overnight or for at least 2 hours.
Eat the softened figs as a snack.
The soaking water can also be consumed for added benefit.
For seed sprinkle: Grind flaxseeds fresh; sprinkle over soaked figs before eating.

recipe_name: Fresh Beetroot Sticks with Pumpkin Seed Sprinkle
description:
Raw beetroot cut into sticks and eaten with a squeeze of lemon as a detox snack.
Beetroot's iron and folate improve scalp circulation and oxygen delivery to hair follicles, directly reducing hair fall.
Its betacyanin pigment is a powerful antioxidant that supports skin cell regeneration and helps fade pigmentation. Pumpkin seeds add zinc for keratin production, complementing beetroot's iron and folate for scalp circulation and hair fall reduction.
preparation_steps: Peel and cut the beetroot into thin sticks.
Squeeze lemon juice over the top.
Eat fresh as a crunchy snack.
For seed sprinkle: Arrange beetroot sticks on a plate; sprinkle pumpkin seeds over the top with lemon juice.

recipe_name: Soaked Raisins with Sesame Seed Sprinkle
description:
A small portion of soaked raisins is a natural iron-rich snack.
Raisins are a concentrated source of iron and B-vitamins that support scalp circulation and reduce hair fall.
Their antioxidants support a healthy gut and help reduce skin breakouts linked to poor digestion. Sesame seeds add calcium and copper for natural hair pigmentation and reduced greying, complementing raisins' iron for scalp circulation.
preparation_steps: Soak raisins in water for 30 minutes until plump.
Drain and eat as a snack.
The soaking water can also be consumed.
For seed sprinkle: Toast sesame seeds lightly; mix with soaked raisins before eating.

recipe_name: Fresh Carrot Sticks with Pumpkin Seed Sprinkle
description:
Raw carrot sticks is  a crunchy beta-carotene-rich snack.
Carrot's beta-carotene converts to vitamin A in the body, supporting skin cell renewal and helping maintain a healthy, even complexion.
Its antioxidants also protect hair follicles from oxidative stress, supporting healthier hair growth over time. Pumpkin seeds add zinc for hair follicle health, complementing carrot's beta-carotene that converts to Vitamin A for skin cell renewal.
preparation_steps: Peel and cut the carrot into sticks.
Squeeze lemon juice over if preferred.
Eat fresh as a crunchy snack.
For seed sprinkle: Arrange carrot sticks; sprinkle pumpkin seeds alongside with lemon juice.

recipe_name: Soaked Cashews
description:
A small portion of soaked cashews is  a zinc and copper-rich snack.
Cashews are one of the best dietary sources of copper and zinc, both of which support melanin production in hair follicles to maintain natural hair colour.
Their healthy fats and vitamin E also support skin barrier integrity and help maintain a smooth, hydrated complexion.
preparation_steps: Soak cashews in water for 2 hours to improve digestibility.
Drain and eat slowly as a snack.

recipe_name: Pistachios
description:
A small handful of pistachios is  a protein and antioxidant-rich snack.
Pistachios provide biotin, vitamin B6 and zinc, all essential for healthy hair growth, reducing hair fall and supporting keratin structure.
Their resveratrol and vitamin E content protect skin cells from free radical damage, supporting a youthful, healthy complexion.
preparation_steps: Shell the pistachios if not already done.
Eat slowly as a snack.
Choose unsalted pistachios for best results.

recipe_name: Brazil Nuts
description:
One to two Brazil nuts is  the most selenium-concentrated food snack.
Brazil nuts are the single richest source of selenium   just one nut provides the daily requirement   protecting hair follicles from oxidative damage.
Selenium also supports thyroid function, hormonal balance and skin antioxidant defence, contributing to clearer, healthier skin.
preparation_steps: Eat 1–2 Brazil nuts as a snack.
Do not exceed 2 per day due to high selenium content.

recipe_name: Fresh Kiwi Fruit with Flaxseed Sprinkle
description:
A single fresh kiwi fruit is  a vitamin C and vitamin K-rich snack.
Kiwi's exceptional vitamin C content boosts collagen synthesis for firmer, more elastic skin and helps fade pigmentation.
Its vitamin E and antioxidants also protect hair follicles from oxidative stress, supporting reduced hair fall and improved scalp health. Ground flaxseeds add plant omega-3 fatty acids that nourish hair follicles, complementing kiwi's dual Vitamin C and Vitamin E for collagen synthesis and skin barrier protection.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Fine lines & ageing, Collagen boost)
preparation_steps: Peel the kiwi or cut in half and scoop out the flesh.
Eat fresh as a snack.
For seed sprinkle: Halve the kiwi; scoop flesh into a bowl; sprinkle ground flaxseeds over the top.

recipe_name: Watermelon Slices with Pumpkin Seed Sprinkle
description:
A small bowl of fresh watermelon slices is  a hydrating lycopene-rich snack.
Watermelon's lycopene is a powerful skin antioxidant that protects against UV-related oxidative damage and supports an even, clear complexion.
Its high water content deeply hydrates skin cells, contributing to a plump, dewy appearance. Pumpkin seeds add zinc for keratin production and hair follicle health, complementing watermelon's lycopene for UV protection and skin hydration.
preparation_steps: Cut watermelon into slices or cubes.
Eat fresh and chilled as a snack.
For seed sprinkle: Arrange watermelon slices; sprinkle roasted pumpkin seeds over the top before eating.

recipe_name: Soaked Walnuts and Figs Combo
description:
A small combination of soaked walnuts and soaked figs eaten together as a hair and skin repair snack.
Walnuts' omega-3 fatty acids reduce skin inflammation, while figs' iron supports scalp circulation to reduce hair fall.
Together they provide a balanced mix of healthy fats, iron, zinc and B-vitamins for comprehensive skin and hair nourishment.
preparation_steps: Soak walnuts in water for 2 hours; soak figs overnight.
Drain both and eat together as a snack.

recipe_name: Mixed Seeds Blend
description:
A small blend of pumpkin, sunflower and flaxseeds is  a skin and hair mineral snack.
Pumpkin seeds provide zinc for keratin production, sunflower seeds deliver vitamin E for skin protection and flaxseeds add omega-3s to reduce skin inflammation.
Together this seed blend covers the key micronutrient gaps for comprehensive hair follicle strength and skin barrier repair.
preparation_steps: Lightly roast pumpkin and sunflower seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes; cool.
Freshly grind the flaxseeds.
Combine all three in a small bowl.
Eat as a snack.

recipe_name: Sweet Potato Collagen Chaat Bowl
description: A vibrant evening chaat combining roasted sweet potato, sprouted moong, beaten egg and tangy chutneys with roasted peanuts.Sweet potato's beta-carotene converts to vitamin A for skin cell renewal, while sprouted moong and egg together deliver plant protein, biotin and zinc essential for hair keratin repair.
preparation_steps: Toss sweet potato cubes with ½ tsp olive oil and a pinch of salt; roast in an oven at 200°C for 20 minutes until golden and tender, or cook in an air fryer for 12–15 minutes.
Boil the sprouted moong dal in water for 5 minutes until just tender; drain and set aside.
Scramble the beaten egg in a non-stick pan with a few drops of oil until just set; break into small pieces.
For the tamarind-date chutney, blend tamarind pulp, dates, cumin powder and water until smooth.
For the coriander chutney, blend coriander leaves, green chili, ginger and lemon juice with water until smooth.
Assemble the chaat   place roasted sweet potato and boiled sprouted moong in a bowl.
Top with scrambled egg pieces and roasted peanuts.
Drizzle tamarind-date chutney and coriander chutney over the top.
Sprinkle with chaat masala and lemon juice.
Serve immediately.

recipe_name: Crunchy Lauki Paneer Cutlets with Chia Raita and Pomegranate Salad
description: Paneer's protein and bottle gourd's high water content work together to support skin hydration and collagen repair, while chia seeds in the raita add omega-3 fatty acids that reduce skin inflammation overnight.Pomegranate's polyphenols fight free radical skin damage
primary_goal: Skin repair (Fine lines & ageing, Pores & texture)
preparation_steps: Grate the bottle gourd and squeeze out all excess water firmly using a clean cloth or your hands   this is essential so the cutlets hold their shape.
Combine grated lauki, grated paneer, onion, green chili, coriander, cumin powder, turmeric, flour and salt in a bowl; mix well.
Divide into 2 equal portions and shape into flat round cutlets.
Heat a non-stick pan with ½ tsp olive oil on medium heat; place the cutlets and cook for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp on both sides.
For the chia raita, soak chia seeds in 1 tbsp water for 10 minutes until gel-like; stir into curd with cumin powder and salt.
For the salad, combine pomegranate arils, sliced onion and diced cucumber in a bowl; toss with black pepper and lemon juice; garnish with coriander.
Plate the cutlets alongside the chia raita and pomegranate salad.
Serve immediately while the cutlets are still warm and crisp.

recipe_name: Iron Boost Laddo
description: A no-cook energy ball combining cashews, sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, soft dates, raisins and amla powder, packed with iron and antioxidants.Dates and raisins provide concentrated iron that improves scalp circulation and reduces hair fall, while sesame seeds and pumpkin seeds add zinc and copper essential for keratin production and natural hair pigmentation.Amla powder's exceptional vitamin C content boosts iron absorption and collagen synthesis, supporting firmer skin and stronger hair follicles.
preparation_steps: Lightly dry roast cashews, sesame seeds and pumpkin seeds in a pan on low heat for 2–3 minutes until fragrant; cool completely.
In a blender, blend the soft dates and raisins together into a sticky paste   no water needed.
Transfer the date-raisin paste into a bowl.
Add the roasted cashews, sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, amla powder and cardamom powder.
Mix everything together thoroughly with clean hands until well combined.
Divide the mixture into 2 equal portions and roll into smooth balls.
If the mixture is too dry, add 1–2 more raisins or a drop of warm water; if too wet, add a pinch more sesame seeds.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.
Serve 2 ladoos per portion at room temperature.

recipe_name: Blueberry Antioxidant Smoothie with Pumpkin Seed Sprinkle
description: Rich in anthocyanins   the most potent antioxidants found in any fruit. Blueberries protect skin collagen from free-radical breakdown while yogurt's probiotics strengthen the gut-skin axis for clearer, glowing skin. Pumpkin seeds add zinc for keratin production, complementing blueberry anthocyanins for skin collagen protection and yogurt's probiotics for gut-skin health.
preparation_steps: Add blueberries, yogurt, honey and water to a blender.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Stir in amla powder after blending.
Drink immediately.
For seed sprinkle: Pour smoothie into a glass; sprinkle pumpkin seeds on top before drinking.

recipe_name: Warm Milk with Honey, Cloves & Cinnamon
description: Warm milk provides tryptophan for restful sleep; cloves deliver eugenol with powerful antibacterial action; cinnamon balances blood sugar to prevent hormonal acne.
preparation_steps: Warm milk in a saucepan on low heat   do not boil.
Add cloves (whole) and cinnamon; simmer 3–4 minutes.
Strain into a cup, removing whole cloves.
Stir in honey once slightly cooled.
Sip slowly.

recipe_name: Kiwi Lemonade with Chia Seed Sprinkle
description: Kiwi provides the most complete Vitamin C + Vitamin E pairing of any single fruit   a rare duo that simultaneously boosts collagen synthesis and protects the skin barrier from oxidative damage. Chia seeds add plant omega-3 and gel-forming fibre that support scalp hydration and the gut-skin axis, complementing kiwi's Vitamin C and Vitamin E.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Fine lines & ageing, Collagen boost)
preparation_steps: Blend kiwi with ¼ cup water until smooth.
Strain into a glass; add remaining water.
Stir in lemon juice, honey and mint leaves.
Drink immediately on an empty stomach.
For seed sprinkle: Soak chia seeds for 15 minutes; stir into the kiwi lemonade before drinking.

recipe_name: Cortisol-Reducing Drink
description: Hibiscus is scientifically shown to lower cortisol   the stress hormone that directly triggers hair fall and acne flare-ups. Coconut water electrolytes replenish adrenal minerals depleted by chronic stress. A pinch of salt prevents electrolyte imbalance.
preparation_steps: Steep hibiscus tea bag and dried flowers in ½ cup hot water for 5–6 minutes.
Remove tea bag; let cool to room temperature.
Stir in coconut water and honey.
Add a pinch of pink salt and stir.
Drink at room temperature or chilled.

recipe_name: Beetroot Chaat with Pumpkin Seed Sprinkle
description: Beetroot is the richest plant source of dietary nitrates, which convert to nitric oxide in the body   directly expanding blood vessels and improving oxygen delivery to skin and scalp cells. Its iron + folate combination fights anaemia-related hair fall and skin dullness. Pumpkin seeds add zinc for keratin production, perfectly complementing beetroot's iron and folate for scalp circulation and reduced hair fall.
preparation_steps: Boil beetroot until fork-tender; cool and peel.
Cut into bite-sized cubes.
Toss with lemon juice, chaat masala, cumin powder and black salt.
Garnish with fresh coriander and pomegranate arils.
Serve immediately at room temperature.
For seed sprinkle: Prepare beetroot chaat as usual; sprinkle roasted pumpkin seeds on top before serving.

recipe_name: Sliced Apple with Nut Butter
description: Apple's quercetin fights skin inflammation while its fibre feeds gut microbiome   improving the gut-skin axis. Almond butter provides biotin (Vitamin B7) for hair keratin strength and Vitamin E for skin barrier repair. One of the most balanced skin + hair snacks available.
preparation_steps: Wash and core the apple; slice into even wedges.
Arrange on a plate.
Serve with almond butter in a small bowl for dipping.
Dust with cinnamon and chia seeds if using.
Eat immediately to prevent browning.

recipe_name: Sweet Corn Chaat with Pumpkin Seed Sprinkle
description: Sweet corn provides lutein and zeaxanthin   antioxidants that protect skin from UV-induced damage and support skin cell renewal. Bell peppers add Vitamin C for collagen synthesis. A fibre-rich, anti-inflammatory snack that supports the gut-skin axis. Pumpkin seeds add zinc and magnesium for hair follicle health, complementing sweet corn's lutein for UV skin protection and collagen support.
preparation_steps: Boil corn kernels until tender; drain and cool.
Combine corn with chopped onion, tomato and capsicum in a bowl.
Add lemon juice, chaat masala and black salt.
Toss well to coat all ingredients.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve immediately.
For seed sprinkle: Prepare sweet corn chaat as usual; sprinkle pumpkin seeds on top before serving.

recipe_name: Cucumber Peanut Salad with Mixed Seed Sprinkle
description: Cucumber's silica content supports collagen and skin elasticity from within while its high water content (96%) deeply hydrates skin cells. Peanuts provide resveratrol   the same anti-ageing antioxidant found in red wine   along with niacin for skin barrier repair. Mixed seeds add zinc and Vitamin E that protect skin cells from oxidative stress and support keratin production, complementing cucumber's silica for skin elasticity.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Hydration, Fine lines, Barrier repair)
preparation_steps: Wash and chop cucumber into bite-sized pieces; no need to peel.
Coarsely crush roasted peanuts.
Combine cucumber, peanuts, coriander and green chilli in a bowl.
Dress with lemon juice, cumin powder, salt and pepper.
Toss well and serve immediately   do not let sit, cucumber releases water.
For seed sprinkle: Prepare cucumber peanut salad as usual; sprinkle mixed seeds on top before serving.

recipe_name: Grilled Paneer with Mint Chutney
description: Paneer (Indian cottage cheese) provides the highest natural protein per bite of any vegetarian food   directly supplying amino acids for hair keratin production. Its proline and lysine content specifically support skin collagen synthesis. Mint chutney adds iron and Vitamin C.
primary_goal: Hair repair (Protein, Keratin strength, Hair fall)
preparation_steps: Mix curd, turmeric, red chilli, garam masala, lemon juice and salt into a marinade.
Coat paneer pieces generously; marinate 20–30 minutes.
Heat a non-stick grill pan on medium-high; brush with olive oil or ghee.
Grill paneer 2–3 minutes per side until golden with char marks.
Serve immediately with fresh mint chutney.

recipe_name: Roasted Sweet Potato with Hung Curd and Pumpkin Seed Sprinkle
description: Sweet potato is one of the richest beta-carotene sources available   converting to Vitamin A in the body to support rapid skin cell turnover (natural retinol effect). Hung curd provides complete protein and probiotics, strengthening both hair follicles and the gut-skin axis simultaneously. Pumpkin seeds add zinc for keratin production, complementing sweet potato's beta-carotene for skin cell renewal and hung curd's protein for hair follicle strength.
preparation_steps: Preheat oven to 200°C (or use an air fryer at 180°C).
Toss sweet potato cubes with olive oil, cumin, paprika and salt.
Spread on a baking tray; roast 20–25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden.
Whisk hung curd with lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Place roasted sweet potato on a plate; dollop hung curd generously.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve warm.
For seed sprinkle: Prepare roasted sweet potato with hung curd as usual; sprinkle pumpkin seeds on top before serving.

recipe_name: Moong dal sprouts
description: Moong sprouts contain the highest plant protein of any sprout   and sprouting multiplies Vitamin C content by 300%, enabling maximum iron absorption from the sprouts themselves. This combination provides all amino acids needed for collagen and hair keratin production.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Glow, Collagen synthesis, Anti-aging) Hair repair (Protein, Hair fall)
preparation_steps: Wash and drain moong sprouts; steam lightly for 2–3 minutes if preferred softer (optional   raw is fine).
Combine sprouts with chopped onion, tomato, cucumber and capsicum.
Add lemon juice, chaat masala and black salt.
Toss well to coat all ingredients.
Garnish with fresh coriander; serve immediately.

recipe_name: High-Protein Oats Chana Tikki
description: A power-packed protein snack combining two complete plant proteins: chickpeas provide all essential amino acids for hair keratin and skin collagen, while oats add beta-glucan   a clinically proven cholesterol reducer that also feeds skin-supporting gut bacteria. Together they deliver a sustained amino acid supply for hair and skin repair.
primary_goal: Hair repair (Protein, Keratin strength, Hair fall)
preparation_steps: Coarsely mash boiled chickpeas   keep some texture, do not over-mash.
Mix in oats, onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander, cumin, garam masala, lemon juice and salt.
Shape into 2 flat round tikkis.
Heat a non-stick pan on medium; brush with olive oil.
Cook tikkis 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Serve hot with mint chutney or hung curd dip.

recipe_name: Moong Dal Khichdi with Cucumber Raita
description:
A one-pot comforting rice and moong dal khichdi tempered with cumin and turmeric, served with a cooling cucumber raita.
Moong dal's easily digestible plant protein and zinc support hair follicle strength and collagen repair for skin.
Curd's probiotics in the raita support gut health, which is directly linked to clearer, calmer skin.
preparation_steps: Wash rice and moong dal together.
In a pot, heat ghee, add cumin seeds and ginger; sauté for 30 seconds.
Add rice, moong dal, turmeric and 2 cups water; bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on low heat for 15–18 minutes until soft and porridge-like.
Mix curd, grated cucumber and cumin powder for the raita.
Serve khichdi hot with cucumber raita.

recipe_name: Ragi Porridge with Boiled Egg and Cucumber Salad
description:
A warm, comforting finger-millet porridge cooked in water and lightly seasoned, served with a boiled egg.
Ragi's calcium and iron strengthen hair roots and prevent premature greying, while egg protein supports keratin rebuilding for hair.
The combination provides a gentle, easily digestible dinner that supports gut health linked to clearer skin.
preparation_steps: Mix ragi flour with ¼ cup water to a smooth lump-free paste.
Bring remaining water to a boil with cumin seeds and ginger.
Slowly stir in the ragi paste and cook on low heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring continuously.
Season with salt.
Boil the egg separately, peel and halve.
Serve the warm ragi porridge with the boiled egg.
Toss cucumber with lemon juice; serve alongside.

recipe_name: Vegetable Sambar Rice (One Pot)
description:
A one-pot sambar rice cooked with toor dal, mixed vegetables and sambar powder for a complete, easy dinner.
Toor dal provides folate and plant protein supporting hair growth and reducing hair fall.
Mixed vegetables deliver antioxidants and vitamin A that support skin cell renewal and a healthy complexion.
preparation_steps: Wash rice and dal together.
Heat oil in a pot, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Add vegetables, turmeric and sambar powder; sauté for 2 minutes.
Add rice, dal, tamarind pulp and 2 cups water; mix well.
Bring to a boil, cover and cook on low heat for 18–20 minutes.
Serve hot.

recipe_name: Spinach Moong Dal Soup with Whole Wheat Roti
description:
A warming iron-rich spinach and moong dal soup served with a simple whole wheat roti.
Spinach's iron and folate improve scalp circulation, directly reducing hair fall and supporting hair regrowth.
Moong dal's zinc and plant protein support collagen synthesis for skin repair and firmer, clearer skin.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Collagen boost, Fine lines & ageing)
preparation_steps: Cook moong dal with turmeric in 1½ cups water until soft (15 minutes on medium heat).
Add spinach and garlic; simmer for 5 minutes until wilted.
Blend partially for a chunky soup; season with salt.
Temper cumin seeds in ½ tsp oil and stir through.
Knead wheat flour with warm water into a soft dough; roll into a thin roti and cook on a dry tawa for 2 minutes per side.
Serve the soup with the roti.

recipe_name: Idli with Coconut Chutney, Tomato Rasam and Cucumber Salad and Soaked Walnuts
description:
Soft steamed idlis served with coconut chutney and a light, digestive tomato rasam   a classic easy dinner.
The fermented idli batter supports gut health, which reflects in clearer, calmer skin over time.
Tomato rasam's vitamin C boosts iron absorption and collagen production, supporting skin firmness and scalp health.
Soaked walnuts as a light snack add plant omega-3 fatty acids that reduce skin inflammation and nourish hair follicles, perfectly rounding out this light fermented dinner.
preparation_steps: Steam idlis from ready batter for 10–12 minutes.
Blend coconut, green chili and ginger with water into a smooth chutney; temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Simmer tomato, tamarind, pepper and cumin in 1 cup water for 10 minutes; strain for the rasam.
Serve hot idlis with coconut chutney and rasam.
Toss cucumber with lemon juice; serve alongside idli.
Serve soaked walnuts as a light side snack   rich in omega-3 fatty acids that reduce skin inflammation and nourish hair follicles.

recipe_name: Oats and Vegetable Khichdi with Carrot-Cucumber Salad and Soaked Almonds
description:
A quick one-pot oats and vegetable khichdi tempered with mustard seeds and turmeric, a light and filling dinner.
Oats provide silica and B-vitamins that strengthen hair strands and support scalp health.
Mixed vegetables add vitamin A and fibre, supporting skin cell renewal and gut health linked to clearer skin.
Soaked almonds as a light snack add biotin (Vitamin B7) and Vitamin E that strengthen hair strands and protect the skin barrier from oxidative damage.
preparation_steps: Heat oil in a pot, temper mustard seeds, curry leaves, ginger and turmeric.
Add carrot and peas; sauté for 2 minutes.
Add water and bring to a boil.
Stir in oats, cover and cook on low heat for 5 minutes until soft.
Season with salt and serve hot.
Mix grated carrot and cucumber with lemon juice; serve alongside.
Serve soaked almonds as a light side snack   biotin and Vitamin E from almonds strengthen hair strands and protect the skin barrier.

recipe_name: Egg Drop Rasam Soup with Brown Rice and Tomato-Onion Salad
description:
A light, peppery tomato rasam with a gently poached egg, served with a small portion of brown rice.
Egg protein and selenium support hair keratin rebuilding and protect the scalp from oxidative damage.
Rasam's black pepper and cumin boost nutrient absorption and provide anti-inflammatory benefits for calmer skin.
preparation_steps: Simmer tomato, tamarind, pepper, cumin and garlic in 1 cup water for 10 minutes.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in ½ tsp oil and stir through.
Bring the rasam to a gentle simmer; crack the egg directly into it and cook for 3–4 minutes until the white is set.
Serve over a small portion of cooked brown rice.
Toss tomato and onion with lemon juice and coriander; serve alongside.

recipe_name: Paneer and Vegetable Soup with Roti and Cucumber Salad
description:
A light paneer and mixed vegetable clear soup, seasoned with cumin and black pepper, served with a whole wheat roti.
Paneer's protein supports collagen and keratin rebuilding for both skin and hair repair.
The mixed vegetables deliver vitamin C and antioxidants that boost skin cell renewal and protect hair follicles.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Fine lines & ageing, Collagen boost)
preparation_steps: Heat oil in a pot, sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Add carrot, beans, cumin and pepper; cook for 2 minutes.
Add water and simmer for 10 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Add paneer cubes and simmer for 3 minutes; season with salt.
Knead wheat flour with warm water; roll and cook roti on a dry tawa for 2 minutes per side.
Serve the soup with the roti.
Toss cucumber with lemon juice and black salt; serve alongside.

recipe_name: Millet Porridge with Sautéed Spinach and Carrot Salad and Fresh Pomegranate Arils
description:
A light, savory foxtail millet porridge cooked with cumin and ginger, served with a quick garlic-sautéed spinach.
Millet's iron and B-vitamins support scalp circulation and hair follicle strength, reducing hair fall.
Spinach's iron and vitamin K support skin repair and circulation, contributing to a healthier, clearer complexion.
Fresh pomegranate arils as a light snack add polyphenols and ellagic acid that protect skin collagen from breakdown and fight free radical skin damage.
preparation_steps: Heat ½ tsp oil in a pot, temper cumin seeds and ginger.
Add millet, turmeric and water; bring to a boil, cover and cook on low heat for 15 minutes until soft and creamy.
Heat ½ tsp oil in another pan, add garlic and spinach; sauté for 3 minutes until wilted.
Season both with salt and serve together.
Toss grated carrot with lemon juice; serve alongside.
Serve pomegranate arils as a light side snack   polyphenols and ellagic acid protect skin collagen and fight free radical skin damage.

recipe_name: Masoor Dal Soup with Brown Rice  and paneer curry
description:
A warming one-pot dinner of red lentil soup and brown rice paired with a lightly spiced paneer curry — simple, quick and ready in under 30 minutes.

Masoor dal's iron and folate improve scalp circulation and directly reduce hair fall, while its easily digestible plant protein supports collagen synthesis for clearer, firmer skin.

Paneer's complete amino acid profile rebuilds hair keratin and provides proline and lysine specifically needed for skin collagen repair and barrier strength.
preparation_steps: For masoor dal soup:
Masoor dal (red lentils) – ½ cup (80 g)
Tomato – ½ cup, chopped (75 g)
Onion – ¼ cup, chopped (30 g)
Garlic – 1 clove, crushed
Ginger – ¼ inch, grated (3 g)
Cumin seeds – ¼ tsp
Turmeric – ¼ tsp
Black pepper – ¼ tsp
Olive oil – ½ tsp (3 mL)
Water – 1½ cups (360 mL)
Salt – to taste
For brown rice:
Brown rice – ½ cup, cooked (100 g)
For paneer curry:
Low-fat paneer – 80 g, cubed
Onion – ¼ cup, finely chopped (30 g)
Tomato – ¼ cup, chopped (30 g)
Ginger-garlic paste – ½ tsp
Turmeric – ¼ tsp
Red chili powder – ¼ tsp
Coriander powder – ¼ tsp
Garam masala – ¼ tsp
Olive oil – ½ tsp (3 mL)
Water – ¼ cup (60 mL)
Fresh coriander leaves – 1 tbsp, chopped

recipe_name: Broccoli and Moong Dal Soup with Cucumber-Tomato Salad and Soaked Almonds and Pumpkin Seeds
description:
A warming, nutrient-dense soup combining broccoli florets with cooked moong dal, blended smooth.
Broccoli's vitamin C and sulforaphane support collagen synthesis and protect skin cells from oxidative damage.
Moong dal adds plant protein and zinc, supporting hair follicle strength and reducing hair fall.
Soaked almonds and pumpkin seeds as a light snack add biotin and zinc   the two most critical nutrients for hair keratin production and skin cell regeneration.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Fine lines & ageing, Collagen boost)
preparation_steps: Heat oil, sauté onion and garlic for 2 minutes.
Add broccoli, moong dal and water; bring to a boil.
Simmer for 15 minutes until broccoli and dal are soft.
Blend until smooth; stir in black pepper and season with salt.
Serve hot.
Toss cucumber and tomato with lemon juice; serve alongside.
Serve soaked almonds and roasted pumpkin seeds as a light snack alongside   biotin from almonds and zinc from pumpkin seeds are essential for hair keratin and skin repair.

recipe_name: Tomato Egg Rice with raita
description:
A quick one-pot tomato-tempered rice tossed with scrambled egg, served with a cooling cucumber raita — under 25 minutes, one pan, minimal cleanup.

Tomato's lycopene protects skin collagen from UV-related free radical breakdown while its Vitamin C boosts iron absorption from the egg for improved scalp circulation and reduced hair fall.

Egg's biotin and complete amino acid profile directly rebuilds hair keratin strand by strand, while curd's probiotics in the raita strengthen the gut-skin axis for clearer, less acne-prone skin.
preparation_steps: Cook brown rice with 1 cup water until fluffy; cool slightly and spread to prevent clumping; set aside (or use pre-cooked rice).
Heat olive oil in a wide pan on medium heat; add mustard seeds and let them splutter; add curry leaves, garlic and ginger; sauté 30 seconds.
Add onion and sauté 3 minutes until translucent; add tomato, turmeric and red chili powder; cook 4–5 minutes until tomato breaks down and masala thickens.
Push the masala to one side of the pan; pour beaten eggs into the cleared space; scramble gently on low heat until just set but still soft; break into small pieces and fold into the masala.

recipe_name: Palak Dosa with Sambar and Chutney
description: Spinach (palak) blended into the dosa batter delivers iron, folate and Vitamin K directly into every bite   the iron-Vitamin C combination in the dosa maximises its own absorption. Sambar's lentil base provides complete plant protein; the fermented dosa batter supplies probiotics for gut-skin health. Coconut chutney adds lauric acid for antimicrobial skin protection.
primary_goal: Skin repair (Collagen, Iron, Gut-skin clarity, Anti-inflammatory)
Hair repair (Iron, Folate, Protein, Hair fall)
preparation_steps: Blend spinach, green chilli and ginger with 2 tbsp water into a smooth purée.
Mix spinach purée thoroughly into dosa batter with salt until evenly green.
For sambar: pressure cook toor dal; sauté onion and tomato in oil; add tamarind water, sambar powder and cooked dal; simmer 10 minutes. Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves.
For chutney: blend coconut, green chilli, ginger, chana dal and lemon juice with water to a smooth paste. Temper with oil, mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Heat a tawa; pour one ladle of palak batter; spread into a thin round.
Drizzle ¼ tsp oil on edges; cook until crisp and edges lift (2–3 minutes).
Serve 2 palak dosas with sambar and coconut chutney.
